Jordan / Samira — thanks, answering each of your asks and including recommended commercial paths below. Attaching SOW for your legal/procurement review (SOW-Acme-2026.docx).

1) Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace as a SaaS offer. Customers can subscribe via marketplace, however many enterprise buyers still require a PO & SOW for internal approvals. If Acme buys via marketplace, billing flows depend on your Cloud Marketplace terms; we can provide a marketplace invoice to reconcile. Link: https://marketplace.cloud/acme/redwood

2) Billing/PO: We can accept PO with Net30. Finance/legal will need the signed SOW and purchase order. If you prefer, we can process a marketplace order and then issue an invoice that your finance team can reconcile.

3) Deployment/packaging options (high-level):
- Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest to production, usage-based pricing (on-demand). Pros: lowest time-to-value, continuous updates, built-in logging. Cons: data lives in multi-tenant service (we provide controls and retention options).
- Dedicated (Reserved GPU pool) — predictability and data isolation within a dedicated cluster. Pricing: commit tiers (monthly/annual) with discounts vs on-demand. Pros: cost predictability and performance SLAs; supports customer-specific isolation.
- Private (VPC / customer-managed) — full isolation, can support customer KMS/HSM and region locking. Pricing: enterprise licensing + deployment fees; supports stronger compliance requirements.

Recommended paths based on your needs: 
A) If you want fastest path and lower up-front cost: Hosted on-demand + standard retention + PO (Net30).
B) If you need predictable costs and some isolation: Dedicated commit (6–12 month) with a commit discount and PO + SOW.
C) If you require KMS and strict residency: Private deployment (we'll involve PM and infra). This usually follows enterprise licensing and longer procurement timelines.

Attachments: SOW-Acme-2026.docx (stub). I've also attached the pricing options PDF earlier that shows example commit tiers.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan: confirm whether you want Redwood to prepare a formal quote for path A/B/C so your PO can reference a specific SKU.
- Marissa / Neha: I'll put Acme on a procurement timeline once they confirm preferred path.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
